title: Path-Enhanced Contrastive Learning for Recommendation

summary: The printed temporal sampler fails its own domain/order guarantee. Its contrastive derivative identities are wrong, while the rotation interpretation requires a normalization qualification.

source_checks.note: Read identity, time-gap transition, temporal guarantee, complex-coordinate update, losses and displayed shared normalizers.

problems.title: Temporal transition is undefined and permits past edges
claim: The sampler uses softmax logits \(w(u,v)/[t(u,v)-t_{\rm last}]\) over the full neighborhood and claims the resulting paths maintain temporal consistency.
analysis: Use one item connected to users at timestamps \(2,1,3\), each with weight \(1\). Follow a valid center prefix whose last timestamp is \(2\). Candidate gaps are \((0,-1,1)\), giving logits \((1/0,-1,1)\), so the printed real-valued transition is undefined. The reverse edge alone produces the zero gap on an undirected graph. Even excluding it leaves positive probability \(1/(1+e^2)\) of selecting timestamp \(1\), violating nondecreasing time.
result: The printed path sampler is neither well-defined on all allowed edges nor sufficient for its temporal-order guarantee. An unstated implementation filter could change the operational behavior, but is not part of the stated formula.
repair: Mask to edges with \(t(u,v)\geq t_{\rm last}\), use a positive offset \(\delta\) in the time-gap denominator, and specify termination or restart when no admissible edge exists. Every retained transition then preserves nondecreasing timestamps.
problems.impact_rationale: The counterexample invalidates the defining temporal-consistency guarantee of the proposed path-generation mechanism.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Contrastive derivatives use the wrong normalizers
problems.source_location: Section 3.5, Eqs.(15)–(18), PDF pp.6–7; objectives (7) and (14)
claim: The displayed gradients give attraction and repulsion the same partition function, summing both positive and denominator exponentials.
analysis: For \(\ell(x)=-\log[A(x)/B(x)]\), direct differentiation gives \(-A^{\prime}(x)/A(x)+B^{\prime}(x)/B(x)\), not a common \(A+B\) denominator. With a self-positive anchor, positive candidate \(1\), negative candidate \(0\) and temperature \(1\), take \(A=e^{x^2}+e^x,B=A+1\). At \(x=0\), the true derivative is \(-1/2+1/3=-1/6\); the printed shared normalizer gives zero. A negative-only denominator does not rescue the formula.
result: The displayed derivative identities and their quantitative weighting interpretation fail. The scalar objectives remain well-defined, and unavailable training code might differentiate those objectives correctly.
repair: Differentiate each log-sum with its own partition function, including candidate/self dependencies and every occurrence in the full loss.
problems.impact_rationale: The explicit analytic derivative is wrong, but this local manuscript derivation does not establish that training used incorrect gradients.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Rotation interpretation depends on normalization
problems.source_location: Section 3.4, Eq.(13), PDF p.6; Appendix A.5, p.23
claim: The paper calls normalized complex-coordinate multiplication a rotation without specifying global or coordinatewise normalization.
analysis: Writing the update as \(T_e(w)=w\odot\overline e\), one has \(\|T_e(w)\|^2=\sum_k|w_k|^2|e_k|^2\). This preserves every distance exactly when every \(|e_k|=1\). Global normalization fixes their squared sum at \(1\), incompatible with that condition in multiple complex coordinates. For real/imaginary halves \(w=(1,0,0,0),e=(1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2)\), the norm contracts from \(1\) to \(1/\sqrt2\).
result: Coordinatewise unit phases validate the multiplicative rotation interpretation. The unspecified normalization leaves a conditional scope qualification; no author-code error or recommendation-performance failure is established.
problems.impact_rationale: The operation is a valid rotation under coordinatewise unit modulus; the source does not resolve the intended normalization.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

impact_rationale: Major: the defining temporal path-sampling guarantee fails on an allowed three-edge interaction graph; the other concerns have narrower scope.
